english: For $k=1,2,\ldots,11$, let $\theta_k=\dfrac{k\pi}{6}$. Then the value of $\displaystyle\sum_{1\le j<k\le 11}\cos\left(\theta_k-\theta_j\right)$ is ______.
hindi: $k=1,2,\ldots,11$ के लिए माना कि $\theta_k=\dfrac{k\pi}{6}$ है। तब $\displaystyle\sum_{1\le j<k\le 11}\cos\left(\theta_k-\theta_j\right)$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Let $S$ be the required sum, $P=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{11}\cos\theta_k$ and $Q=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{11}\sin\theta_k$.

Sum of cosines with angles in AP: $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\cos k\alpha=\frac{\sin\frac{n\alpha}{2}}{\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}}\cos\frac{(n+1)\alpha}{2}$, and similarly for sines with $\sin\dfrac{(n+1)\alpha}{2}$.
(Check by counting: $S=\sum_{d=1}^{10}(11-d)\cos\dfrac{d\pi}{6}$, whose $\sqrt3$ terms cancel, also gives $-5$.)
originality_note: New: the sum of cosines of all 55 pairwise differences of an AP of angles that does NOT close the circle (11 of the 12 directions), evaluated through |sum of unit vectors|^2 and the AP sum formulas (way 4). Closest known: sin a + sin b + sin c = 0 = cos a + cos b + cos c implies sum cos(a - b) = -3/2. Different because: the vector sum is not zero here (P = -1), and it must be found by the AP formula.
blueprint_concepts: Summation of trigonometric series with angles in AP

concept_use.Summation of trigonometric series with a: P = sum cos(k pi/6) = -1 and Q = sum sin(k pi/6) = 0 by the AP sum formulas give 1 = 11 + 2S.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, function and interval is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/mpmath, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. The sum is over unordered pairs j < k (stated by the index set). Changed: No change.
key_step: Writing the pairwise sum through P^2 + Q^2 and evaluating P, Q by AP sums.
justification: One known trick (square of the vector sum) plus two routine AP sums. Numerical but short. Like 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).
